question: Under what condition can anything be called truly existent?
premises: Nothing is called existent without the ascent of will, knowledge, and action.
Existence arises from the ascent of that triad of powers.
That ascent occurs in the Bhairava-conscious self.
inference: Therefore true existence depends on the activity of the three powers within consciousness.
uncertainties: bhairavīye cidātmani could be taken as a locative description or as a more technical doctrinal designation.
plain_english: Nothing can be called truly existent without the ascent of will, knowledge, and action. Such existence arises only from the ascent of that triad of powers in the Bhairava-conscious self.
